Switzerland / PLANNING GUIDE

Switzerland Travel Planning Guide

Choose a starting city, a season and a manageable route for your Switzerland break.

By Travelber Editorial · Updated 19 October 2026

IN THIS GUIDE

← Switzerland overview

The short version

Switzerland combines lakeside cities, medieval centres and distinctive German-, French- and Italian-speaking regions.

First break2–3 nightsSuggested approachOne baseStart comparingZurich

Choose a starting city

  • Zurich: Zurich combines medieval lanes along the Limmat with lakeside promenades and major art museums.
  • Geneva: Geneva brings together international institutions, a hillside old town and Lake Geneva's waterfront.
  • Basel: Basel pairs a medieval Rhine-side centre with a concentration of art museums.
  • Bern: Bern's arcaded old town occupies a peninsula enclosed by a bend in the Aare.
  • Lucerne: Lucerne combines covered wooden bridges and painted old-town façades beside its Alpine lake.

Compare all ten cities

Match the plan to your stay

For two nights, keep one city as your base. With three or four nights, add a second neighbourhood or a carefully checked day trip. For a longer stay, compare actual journey times before adding another base; the city collection is not a suggested rail circuit.

Choose a season

Scenic transport services have route-specific operating calendars; check boat and mountain connections for your exact travel date.

Keep the route practical

Use SBB for connected rail, bus and boat journeys, and check panoramic trains separately for service-specific seat reservations.

Read the transport guide

Before you book

  • Confirm your arrival station or airport and the last connection to your stay.
  • Choose one priority experience per day.
  • Check entry times and cancellation terms with the venue.
  • Keep an indoor alternative and compare total accommodation costs.
